about: Paras Healthcare runs eight tertiary and quaternary care hospitals under the 'Paras Health' brand across Haryana, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand and Jammu & Kashmir, with 2,211 beds as of June 30, 2026. Cardiac, oncology, neuro, gastro, orthopaedic and renal specialties (CONGOR) made up 74.70% of FY26 revenue from operations. It had 1,084 doctors and 1,937 nurses and plans to add hospitals in Gurugram and Ludhiana.

promoters.background: Promoter and Managing Director; has led the commissioning of all the hospitals over two decades and has over 22 years of healthcare experience. Commelina Ltd (affiliate of Creador) invested in 2017 and is a selling shareholder.

concentration.note: Government schemes and PSUs were 41.28% of FY26 revenue from operations (30.91% in FY25, 29.76% in FY24). Five of eight hospitals in North India gave 66.07% of FY26 revenue.

litigation_note: Contingent liabilities were 89.55% of net worth as of June 30, 2026, including liquidated damages notices to a subsidiary from Heavy Engineering Corporation. A Promoter Group member, Harbaksh Singh Khangura, appears in the CIBIL wilful defaulter database.
strengths: One of the largest healthcare providers in North India, Bihar and Jharkhand with 2,211 beds across eight hospitals and a recognised 'Paras Health' brand.
Focus on high-acuity tertiary and quaternary care: CONGOR specialties gave 74.70% of FY26 revenue from operations.
Revenue from operations grew at a 19.26% CAGR from Rs 1,129.04 crore in FY24 to Rs 1,605.95 crore in FY26.
EBITDA grew from Rs 154.41 crore in FY24 to Rs 335.58 crore in FY26, with margin rising from 13.42% to 20.60%.
Bed occupancy improved from 52.46% in FY24 to 61.75% in FY26 as newer hospitals ramp up.
Seven of eight hospitals are NABH accredited, with 1,084 doctors and 1,937 nurses as of June 30, 2026.
Mix of owned, leased and revenue-share hospitals; capex per bed was Rs 7.70 million as of June 30, 2026.
Committed expansion of a 300-bed Gurugram hospital and a 500-bed Ludhiana hospital, taking capacity to 3,011 beds by March 2028.

risks.title: History of losses
risks.detail: The company lost Rs 15.33 crore in FY24 and Rs 57.98 crore in FY25 on a consolidated basis; profit of Rs 43.83 crore in FY26 may not be sustained.

risks.title: Loss-making subsidiaries
risks.detail: Subsidiaries Paras Healthcare (Ranchi) and Plus Medicare Hospitals lost Rs 87.27 crore in FY24, Rs 82.24 crore in FY25 and Rs 52.09 crore in FY26 collectively.

risks.title: High debt and leverage
risks.detail: Fund-based borrowings were Rs 888.89 crore at June 30, 2026 and debt to equity (including leases) was 3.53 times in FY26 and 4.39 times in FY25.

risks.title: Contingent liabilities
risks.detail: Contingent liabilities were 89.55% of net worth as of June 30, 2026, including liquidated damages claims by Heavy Engineering Corporation on a subsidiary.

risks.title: Dependence on government schemes
risks.detail: Government schemes and PSUs contributed 41.28% of FY26 revenue from operations, up from 29.76% in FY24, which raises payment-delay and tariff risk.

risks.title: Promoter Group member on wilful defaulter list
risks.detail: Promoter Group member Harbaksh Singh Khangura appears in the CIBIL wilful defaulter database in relation to Majestic Hotels Limited defaults from 2014.

risks.title: High staff attrition
risks.detail: Attrition of doctors, nurses and support staff was 60.38% in FY26, 66.74% in FY25 and 65.27% in FY24.

risks.title: Regional and specialty concentration
risks.detail: Five of eight hospitals are in North India (66.07% of FY26 revenue) and CONGOR specialties gave 74.70% of FY26 revenue; six of eight hospitals are on leased premises.

notes: Consolidated, restated; FY24-FY26 audited. Source tables were garbled so figures were cross-checked (net worth = equity + other equity; borrowings = non-current incl. current maturities + current borrowings, excluding lease liabilities; cash_and_bank = cash and equivalents + other bank balances; current ratio computed from total current assets/liabilities; operating cash flow reconciled to investing and financing flows). Q1FY27 (June 30, 2026) stub ignored: revenue Rs 470.28 crore, PAT Rs 49.68 crore, basic EPS Rs 4.92 (not annualised). Price band, P/E, share counts and reservation not yet disclosed in the RHP (shown as blanks); Fresh Issue is Rs 5,000 million and Offer for Sale up to Rs 3,000 million (promoter) plus Rs 6,500 million (Commelina). pre_issue_shares is the share count as at June 30, 2026 (face value Rs 1). Peer revenue converted from Rs million.
